name: Employment-rights implementation change feed
demand: The broad regulated base is 1,417,730 UK private-sector employer businesses at the start of 2025, including 1,150,875 with 1–9 employees; these are not all prospective software buyers ([DBT business population estimates](https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/business-population-estimates-2025/business-population-estimates-for-the-uk-and-regions-2025-statistical-release)). HMRC maintains a recognised payroll-software list, updated 16 October 2026, but does not give a total on that page ([HMRC list](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/find-payroll-software-that-is-recognised-by-hmrc)); a third-party directory counted 127 recognised payroll software companies on 8 January 2026, a dated market-map proxy rather than a current official count ([directory](https://businessfinancing.co.uk/payroll-software/payroll-software-companies/)). Moorepay reports 445 payroll-industry responses to its 2025 survey: 49% wanted more payroll-process automation, while 8% selected API integration as their preferred software approach. This suggests interest in automation but does not validate demand for this feed ([survey and methodology](https://www.moorepay.co.uk/annual-payroll-survey-report-25-26/)). Acas reported 18.5 million page accesses and over 400,000 people trained during 1 April 2025–31 March 2026; that is broad employment-advice interest, not feed demand ([Acas report summary](https://www.acas.org.uk/annual-report-reveals-exceptional-demand-for-acas)). Search-volume, installations, named vendor users, and vendor demand for a separate API: unverified.
prices: No public price found for a vendor-focused commencement feed/API. Adjacent offers show paid employment-compliance products, but not vendor willingness to pay: Employment Hero lists HR and Employment Law Advisory at £6 per employee/month with a £60 minimum ([pricing](https://employmenthero.com/uk/pricing/)); HRConnect lists an Employment Rights Act implementation and training service at £325 plus VAT per organisation ([Spring 2026 catalogue](https://www.hrconnect.org.uk/hubfs/Downloads/External/HR%20Connect/HR%20Connect%20Products%20and%20Services%20Catalogue%20Spring%202026-1.pdf?hsLang=en)); Statuta currently quotes white-label compliance by client-book size without publishing a fixed amount ([product page](https://www.statuta.uk/)). For payroll-software price context, Sage lists Payroll Essentials from £12/month ([Sage](https://www.sage.com/en-gb/products/free-trials/)) and IRIS Staffology lists £43/month for 1–19 payslips ([IRIS](https://www.iris.co.uk/products/staffology-payroll/)). These are asking prices, not evidence of completed sales or feed pricing.
copy_speed: High for public timelines and editorial trackers; no vendor-focused maintained commencement API/feed surfaced in the reviewed results. GOV.UK itself updated its timeline on 22 October 2026 ([latest timeline](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/implementing-the-plan-to-make-work-pay-and-employment-rights-act/plan-to-make-work-and-employment-rights-act-timeline-update)). A free Legal Brief tracker was last updated August 2026 ([tracker](https://thelegalbrief.co.uk/guides/employment-rights-act-implementation-tracker/)); WPC HR published a detailed tracker on 14 October 2026, including separate statuses for confirmed and announced changes ([tracker](https://www.wpchr.co.uk/blog/employment-rights-act-timeline)); and PaySoft labels its ERA-related payroll features as new in April 2026, though it does not publish a release date ([PaySoft](https://paysoft.scot/)). LexiTrove, an adjacent UK employment-law intelligence product, was reported founded on 14 May 2026 and was recruiting pilot firms in July; it is not a vendor date feed ([report](https://legaltechnology.com/startup-corner-lexitrove-ai-for-the-employment-matter-lifecycle/)). Statuta currently describes a product that reviews legal changes and maps them across adviser clients, but its launch date is unverified ([Statuta](https://www.statuta.uk/)).
platform_risk: High raw-data and substitution risk. Legislation.gov.uk already offers free API access to legislation, metadata, changes/effects and Atom feeds, including in-force dates; its documentation permits commercial use and notes the dataset is incomplete and API output can be cached ([API overview](https://legislation.github.io/data-documentation/api/overview.html), [reuse and feeds](https://legislation.github.io/data-documentation/)). The Open Government Licence allows commercial reuse of covered government material ([National Archives guidance](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/re-use-of-public-sector-information-regulations-2015-and-crown-copyright-in-knowledge-asset-commercialisation/re-use-of-public-sector-information-regulations-2015-and-crown-copyright-in-knowledge-asset-commercialisation)). GOV.UK also publishes a free timetable whose future dates can change ([latest timeline](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/implementing-the-plan-to-make-work-pay-and-employment-rights-act/plan-to-make-work-and-employment-rights-act-timeline-update)). A feed outage, stale source, or mislabelled announcement could therefore damage trust in a product whose value depends on current legal status.
defensible_asset: Raw UK legislation and its dates are not proprietary. A plausible asset is a carefully versioned mapping from Act provisions to commencement instruments, including geography, transitional rules, source evidence and an explicit distinction between announced policy dates and dates fixed by law. That interpretation layer and reliable vendor integrations could create some switching cost after adoption; neither the asset nor switching cost exists yet. The distinction matters in the current timetable: SI 2026/559 brings the unfair-dismissal changes into force on 1 January 2027 ([instrument](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/559/made/data.html)); GOV.UK now lists fire-and-rehire protections for March 2027, while section 28’s commencement information shows only partial commencement for specified purposes so far ([latest timetable](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/implementing-the-plan-to-make-work-and-employment-rights-act/plan-to-make-work-and-employment-rights-act-timeline-update), [Act section 28](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2025/36/section/28)).
build_effort: Moderate engineering for a read-only MVP; ongoing legal-status review is the hard part. Existing legislation API feeds can support source monitoring and change detection, while an event store can hold the mapped provision, instrument, effective date, status and evidence URL ([API documentation](https://legislation.github.io/data-documentation/api/overview.html)). Agents could poll, diff, classify and draft records; a human reviewer should verify substantive changes and transitional provisions before publication. The product has not been built, so implementation time, operating cost and reliable automation rate are unverified.
channel: Prefer inbound technical documentation, sample JSON/OpenAPI, search-friendly change notes and an opt-in vendor pilot request. The CIPP has a 2026 payroll-software directory and invites supplier inclusion and sponsorship/advertising ([CIPP directory](https://www.cipp.org.uk/resources/payroll-software-directory.html)). If testing with email, restrict it to verified corporate subscribers and generic company addresses, identify the sender and provide an opt-out; the ICO says sole traders and some partnerships generally need consent or a valid soft opt-in for electronic marketing ([ICO B2B guidance](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/)). Do not use cold messages to individuals or sole traders.
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified. The <=5 hours/week constraint is not evidenced; it depends on low support volume, reliable automated monitoring and human legal review remaining small.
desk_test: One-day, low-cost test: manually produce a static three-event JSON sample with source and status fields: the 1 January unfair-dismissal commencement in SI 2026/559; the March 2027 fire-and-rehire timetable entry clearly labelled as announced rather than fixed by a commencement instrument; and one relevant late-October change with its instrument. Put it beside a one-page vendor-facing explanation and an opt-in pilot request. Distribute through an appropriate CIPP supplier/advertising channel or contact only verified corporate subscribers under ICO rules. Count success only if a payroll/HR software vendor requests integration details and one agrees in writing to a paid pilot; the price and response rate are unverified. Sources: [SI 2026/559](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/559/made/data.html), [latest GOV.UK timeline](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/implementing-the-plan-to-make-work-and-employment-rights-act/plan-to-make-work-and-employment-rights-act-timeline-update), [CIPP directory](https://www.cipp.org.uk/resources/payroll-software-directory.html), [ICO B2B guidance](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/).
red_flags: The lead’s trigger is partly stale as of 23 October 2026: GOV.UK changed fire-and-rehire from the earlier January timetable to March 2027 on 22 October; unlike unfair dismissal, no commencement instrument fixing that fire-and-rehire date was found in the cited legislation record ([latest timetable](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/implementing-the-plan-to-make-work-and-employment-rights-act/plan-to-make-work-and-employment-rights-act-timeline-update), [section 28 commencement information](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2025/36/section/28)). This is evidence for a status-aware tracker, but also demonstrates that free editorial trackers can cover much of the need and become stale. No qualifying transaction, customer count or revenue proof for this API was found; current prices are analogues, not revenue. Vendor demand, automation of at least 50%, and operation within 5 hours/week are all unverified. Lead survives the initial kill-check as a data-product hypothesis, not yet as a validated business.
